newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast gasoline rises amid low supplies.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast gasoline rises amid low supplies.

text.p: U.S. West Coast gasoline prices advanced Tuesday, after a modest build in regional stocks failed to convince traders production would keep pace with demand until mid-April, players said.
Tight supplies of West Coast gasoline rose modestly, up 861,000 barrels last week from an 11-year low of 25.6 million the week before, the American Petroleum Institute reported.

"Prompt gasoline is very tight, probably for the next two weeks until these refineries come back," one trader said, referring to ongoing shutdowns of hydrocracker units at Exxon, Unocal, and Tosco refineries in California.
Mobil Corp's Los Angeles refinery resumed full production over the weekend, the company said, ending a prolonged restart which pushed wholesale gasoline prices up 6.5 cents last week.
CARB-grade gasoline in Los Angeles was done at 86 cents a gallon Tuesday, and traders saw offers as high as 87 cents, up 2.50 cents from Monday levels.
"It's higher than yesterday. Until the major (refineries) stop buying we'll keep going up," one broker said.
Offers for conventional gasoline in L.A. rose 1.50 cents a gallon to 82.50 cents.
Distillate saw smaller gains Tuesday, with jet fuel gaining the most, up 1.50 cents to 63/64 cents.
